requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long
requirements.summary: PAM was configured via /etc/pam.d/base-password with pam_pwquality.so minlen=12 (plus enforce_for_root). Direct tests show a 7-character password ('Short1!') was hard-rejected with 'password is shorter than 12 characters' after enforce_for_root was added, while 12+ character passwords succeeded. Enforcement was re-verified after a full node reboot with a fresh test user.

requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must use at least three different character classes
requirements.summary: minclass=3 was set in pam_pwquality.so config. A 12+ character all-lowercase password (2 classes) was hard-rejected with 'password contains less than 3 character classes' after enforce_for_root was added; a password combining upper/lower/digit classes succeeded. Re-verified after reboot.

requirements.requirement: The password-complexity policy must actually take effect (not merely be written to a config file) and survive a restart
requirements.summary: Initial testing (before enforce_for_root) revealed that pam_pwquality silently exempts root-driven password changes by default, so early weak-password tests misleadingly 'succeeded'; the executor correctly diagnosed this and added enforce_for_root, after which weak passwords were hard-rejected. The node was then rebooted (boot id changed from 3e02fd26… to a96aecdc…, consistent with the global before/after boot-identity snapshots), and post-reboot testing with a fresh test user confirmed the policy file persisted and enforcement still worked (reject short/weak, accept 12+/3-class).

requirements.requirement: Policy should apply to node1 (the only managed node) without unintended cross-node scope issues
requirements.summary: node1 is the sole managed node in this topology; all commands and evidence are scoped to node1 only, consistent with the task's single-node instruction.

overall_summary: The executor correctly implemented and verified a password-complexity policy on node1 requiring 12+ character length and 3+ character classes via pam_pwquality.so (minlen=12, minclass=3), discovering and correcting a subtle root-exemption gap by adding enforce_for_root. The policy's real-world effect was demonstrated with explicit reject/accept tests before and after a full node reboot, with boot-identity evidence confirming the restart occurred and the post-reboot behavior matching the pre-reboot configuration. Temporary test users were cleanly removed; minor leftover temp log files are the only hygiene concern.
limitations: The executor's final report/selected-evidence block referenced a nonexistent command ID ('cmd-1'), so the structured self-report itself is not usable evidence; this assessment relies entirely on the raw command timeline and lifecycle snapshots.

All password-change tests were performed by root modifying another user's password; no test was captured of a genuinely non-root user changing their own password via the passwd prompt, though the pam_pwquality default behavior and enforce_for_root semantics make it reasonable to infer that non-root enforcement functions as tested.
Two temporary log files (/tmp/apkupdate.log, /tmp/reboot.log) were left on node1 after the task; low sensitivity but unaddressed residue.
Executor evidence item 1 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-1

operational_hygiene.summary: Test users pwtestuser and pwverifyuser (bounded, low-risk) were created for validation and both were subsequently removed with deluser --remove-home, with grep checks confirming no leftover entries in /etc/passwd, /etc/group, /etc/shadow, or home directories — a properly restored temporary mutation. The apk add of shadow/libpwquality/cracklib is a necessary, retained prerequisite for the task and not residue. The self-initiated reboot (cmd-0402ef912a9c48a3) was a state-changing action with no explicit basis in the public task contract, but it aligns with the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol and was used constructively to verify policy persistence, so it is not penalized as an unnecessary mutation. Two log files (/tmp/apkupdate.log, /tmp/reboot.log) were left behind after the run and were not cleaned up, per the after-executor temporary-files snapshot — minor, non-sensitive residue that slightly lowers the hygiene score.
